items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis and a short comic pause before each punchline; a touch of wonder on the line about watching it burn. Chars voices funny cartoon characters, short and punchy.
lines: You've probably never seen Hally's Comet.
But right now, pieces of it are hitting your sky.
And Hally itself is over five billion kilometres away.
Rewind. Every seventy-six years, Hally swings close to the Sun.
The heat cooks its ice, and it sheds dust. Lots of it.
[vain, posh, offended cosmic diva, flicking her hair] It's not dandruff. It's a tail.
That dust stays behind, spread all along Hally's path.
So how does it reach your sky?
Hally's path crosses Earth's path. Twice a year.
In May, we clip it. In October, we hit it again.
[weary, exasperated, tired house-proud mum] Again? I just cleaned up in May!
Here's the twist. Hally goes around the Sun the wrong way.
So we hit its dust head-on, at sixty-six kilometres a second.
That's Delhi to Mumbai in about seventeen seconds.
Each grain is about the size of sand.
It burns up around a hundred kilometres above you. About eleven Everests up.
Best seen after midnight, from both halves of the planet.
Most of us have never seen Hally's Comet... But every October, you can watch it burn.
Hally itself is due back in twenty sixty-one.
[weary, exasperated, tired house-proud mum, now flat and deadpan, resigned] Until then, I'll keep driving through its dust.
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
